request.spec:
Give every invoice a number made from its id: INV-, then the id padded to six digits, then a
Luhn check digit worked out over those six digits. For the check digit, start from the
rightmost digit and double every second digit (the rightmost, the third from the right, and
so on), subtract 9 from any doubled result over 9, add all the digits up, and the check digit
is whatever brings the total up to the next multiple of ten (0 if it already is one). So
invoice 7 is INV-0000075. Show the number in the invoice list and at the top of the panel.
Add a box where I can type an invoice number to open that invoice, selecting its client; if
the check digit doesn't match, tell me the number is mistyped and open nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Give every invoice a number made from its id: INV-, then the id padded to six digits, then a
Luhn check digit worked out over those six digits. For the check digit, start from the
rightmost digit and double every second digit (the rightmost, the third from the right, and
so on), subtract 9 from any doubled result over 9, add all the digits up, and the check digit
is whatever brings the total up to the next multiple of ten (0 if it already is one). So
invoice 7 is INV-0000075. Show the number in the invoice list and at the top of the panel.
Add a box where I can type an invoice number to open that invoice, selecting its client; if
the check digit doesn't match, tell me the number is mistyped and open nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every invoice now has a number. It shows in the invoice list and at the top of the invoice panel, and there's a box where you can type a number to open that invoice. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

- **The number:** the server works it out from the invoice id, so nothing new is stored and the database is unchanged. The logic is in `InvoiceNumber.java`. Invoice 7 comes out as INV-0000075 and invoice 4096 as INV-0040964, and a newly created invoice gets its number straight away.
- **Opening by number:** the box sits above the client list. When you submit a number, the server checks the check digit. If it matches, the app selects that invoice's client and opens the invoice in the panel. This goes through a new endpoint, `GET /api/invoices/by-number/{number}`.
- **Wrong numbers:** if the check digit is wrong, you get "INV-… is mistyped: check the invoice number." and nothing opens. If the number is valid but no such invoice exists, it says "There is no invoice INV-…".

Two smaller changes came with this:
- The invoice error handler now returns errors raised by these endpoints as structured error responses, so the page can show the server's message. This also affects the existing "No such invoice" errors.
- If you open an invoice by number and then click a client yourself, the earlier lookup is cleared. Going back to that client won't reopen the looked-up invoice.
